messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-streaming cluster eu-west-1 — p99 latency spike above SLO (6.2s) and increasing error rate. Rule: streaming_tail_latency > 4s for 5m. Affected service: inference-streamer-v2. Paging oncall: @alex. Metric links: https://grafana.redwood/prod/streaming?panel=tail_latency :rotating_light:

alex (oncall): On it. Seeing the same in Grafana. p95 ~ 1.1s -> 1.4s, p99 ~ 6.2s -> 8.0s on some shards. Streaming stalls + partial responses. Customers on high-concurrency routes hit first.

mira (sre): Reproduced traces show a pattern: sudden KV cache evictions + many prefill tasks queued. Prefill workers are faster than decode pipeline, causing KV fragmentation and reads to thrash. Also notice increased io_wait on GPU host during prefill bursts.

alex (oncall): Is this the same kv-prefill vs decode imbalance we saw last month?

mira (sre): Similar but different shape — fragmentation is higher (many small slabbing events). Eviction rate spiked concurrently with a burst of long-context requests. Prefill allocs outpaced decode consumes, so cache churn skyrocketed.

devin (runtime): Logs from one affected shard (shard-12) show repeated prefill write -> immediate eviction -> prefill re-run:

```
2026-03-15T03:22:14Z shard=shard-12 prefill: wrote kv_block id=0x7f3a len=48kb
2026-03-15T03:22:14Z shard=shard-12 evict: removed kv_block id=0x2a9c len=52kb reason=slab_compact
2026-03-15T03:22:15Z shard=shard-12 prefill: miss -> fetch upstream -> write kv_block id=0x8f12 len=49kb
2026-03-15T03:22:15Z shard=shard-12 decode: waiting queue_len=24
```

devin (runtime): That cycle is expensive — prefill writes then eviction forces refetch and stalls decode. Disk IO and NVCache pressure both visible.

alex (oncall): Customer impact? Which tenants/routes?

sam (product): Two customers flagged: rapid-chat Inc (high concurrency), and internal sandbox tests. Rapid-chat saw streaming stalls and a backlog of partial events; SLA p99 breaches for ~7 minutes. No 5xxs but elevated client disconnects.

mira (sre): Immediate mitigation options:
- throttle prefill workers on affected shards (rate-limit prefill per-shard)
- increase eviction threshold/slab headroom temporarily (+20%)
- enable decode-priority scheduling so decoder threads get CPU/GPU priority
- route new streaming traffic to fallback model variant (v2-small-quant) with smaller kv footprint

alex (oncall): Which can we safely do quickly?

devin (runtime): Fastest: flip prefill throttle and enable decode-priority via runtime flags — zero deployment restart, change via admin API. Fallback routing requires route rewrite in router and will take ~5-10m to drain. Increasing slab headroom needs config push and careful monitoring but can be done via feature-flag toggles on the control plane (estimated 3-5m).

alex (oncall): Do it. Steps please and I'll execute and monitor.

devin (runtime): Executing now:
1) POST to /admin/shards/shard-12/actions with {"action":"set_prefill_rate","rate_per_sec":5} -> returns 202
2) POST to /admin/global/actions {"action":"enable_decode_priority", "duration":"15m"} -> returns 200
3) Feature-flag: set feature.kv.slab_headroom.factor=1.2 for prod-streaming -> rolling apply to affected hosts.

ops-bot: Action results: set_prefill_rate accepted for shard-12 (rate=5r/s) ; decode_priority: enabled globally for 15m ; feature flag rollout started (batch=10 hosts).

alex (oncall): Monitoring p99 and streaming success. Initial signal: p99 on shard-12 down from ~8s to ~3.2s within 90s. Error rate trending down.

mira (sre): Nice. Keep an eye on eviction_rate and slab fragmentation metrics. If fragmentation not improving, we should increase slab headroom further or consider a targeted restart of the most fragmented runtimes to defragment memory.

devin (runtime): Noted. Also starting a background job to compact KV slabs more aggressively on low-traffic shards (non-disruptive throttle).

sam (product): I'll send a short customer note: "We identified a transient caching issue causing intermittent streaming stalls; mitigations are in place and performance is returning to normal. Follow-up to come." Want me to send now?

alex (oncall): Yes, send to impacted customers. Use the status template.

ops-bot: Feature flag rollout batch 1 complete (10/50 hosts), batch 2 in progress.

mira (sre): After ~6m overall, p95 ~1.0s, p99 ~1.8s globally. Eviction rate down 62% on affected shards, decode queue back to normal. I recommend we keep decode-priority for an hour and keep prefill throttle at a conservative rate until slab headroom reaches steady-state.

alex (oncall): Agreed. I'll hand this to morning oncall in 45m. Handoff note: incident mitigated, customer-facing message sent, short-term flags: prefill_rate=5r/s for hot shards, decode-priority=enabled (will auto-disable in 1h), slab_headroom factor=1.2. Follow-ups: schedule a postmortem to analyze why prefill burst correlated with fragmentation and to add emergency runbook steps for slab compaction.

mira (sre): I'll own the postmortem and add a checklist: detect prefill/decode imbalance, automated throttle, slab headroom runtime toggle, fallback routing playbook.

alex (oncall): Handoff to @mira. If anything flares, call pager. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mira (sre): Adding notes to the incident page: https://incidents.redwood/4456789012 — will include timeline and graphs.

ops-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated.

alex (oncall): Closing thread from oncall side, handing to SRE for follow-up.
